w: Today was the Pushpadolotsav, the festival of colours. Having coloured about 60,000 devotees with the colour of God, Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to his residence. This time colour had splashed on Swamishri too. His upper cloth and dhoti were wet with colour. In wet clothes Swamishri came to the door. Here volunteers bowed and welcomed him. Swamishri asked them, "Didn't you come to the festival of colours?"
"No. Our seva was here."

"Is that so!" Saying this, Swamishri wrung out his wet upper cloth. He gathered the colour in his right palm and sprinkled it on both of them. There was not much. A few drops, a little spray flew. Both were coloured and felt blessed. The same affection that was on Swamishri's face while colouring 60,000 devotees was there while colouring just two devotees. The colour barely fell on them and disappeared. But their hearts were now dripping, coloured with the colour of love. Not only will these two never forget this incident, but neither will the four or five people standing around. This is what is called an ocean of love in a drop of colour!

At 5.30 p.m. Swamishri left Limbdi and reached Gondal at 8.20 p.m.

Swamishri visited the BAPS cattle camp in Sarangpur. With 2000 cattle in the camp ( details of cattle camps ), and still more arriving, the BAPS is providing care and nourishment to save them from the severe drought that is prevaling in Gujarat. The camp is hosting cattle from the districts of Bhavnagar, Amreli, Surendranagar and Dhandhuka. Everyday the cattle are provided with 10kgs of fodder and nutrients. Swamishri offered fodder to several oxen and also blessed the volunteers and farmers who tend the cattle. Swamishri said: "This is not a cattle ground but a cattle camp that looks after the welfare of animals. This is a great pilgrim place. We go to a pilgrim place for God's darshan and redemption. When you've come to a pilgrim place you have to give up your addictions..."
A little observance of agna gives a huge benefit, and a little disobedience in agna produces a lot of pain and misery.

You will find people who will bless you with money, children and who can fly in the air. But that is not greatness. True greatness lies in engaging ones senses and mind in God, in doing God's bhajan and in being redeemed from the cycles of birth and death and from ignorance.

In the evening assembly, the kishores presented a debate and 'Ruchi Quiz' before Swamishri. Swamishri's participation in the Quiz enthused the kishores and the assembly. Finally, Swamishri addressed the assembly.
Swamishri performed his morning puja in Modhera.
At 7.00 p.m., Swamishri arrived at Limbodra and was pleased to see the period sets of Loj village.
At 6.00 p.m. Swamishri arrived in Lathidad to perform the pujan and arti of the recently inaugurated hari mandir.

At 10.10 am Swamishri departed from Amdavad and arrived at Sarangpur at 12.10 pm. In the evening at 7.10 pm Swamishri blessed 4000 volunteers who had assembled to offer their services for the Fuldol festival. In his blessings Swamishri inspired the volunteers to serve sincerely in the festival. Thereafter Swamishri first sprayed coloured water on Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and then on the volunteers.

At 6.15 a.m. During Swamishri’s puja the rituals continued and thereafter bhajans were sung. At 8.35 a.m, the final part of the diksha rituals commenced. Senior sadhus gave each of the youths a kanthi , upper cloth, pagh, smeared chandan on their forehead, and gave a flower and prasad box to their parents. Swamishri finally administered the diksha mantra. In conclusion, Swamishri blessed all, “To take diksha as a sadhu is a great thing. All praises for their parents for sacrificing their son. This is possible only when one has deep faith in God and the understanding that God looks after everyone and everything. The youths who have become sadhus and parshads must have had great worldly ambitions. They have been brought up abroad in a materialistic culture yet they have left all the attractions. To give this up is a difficult thing. Let us pray that they all become very good sadhus, offer bhakti and inspire others to do so and become happy. May Maharaj bless their parents with happiness and good tidings.”
True goal of life

1 March 2009, Delhi, Bhavnagar Shri Manavsingh runs a business of renting chartered planes. Swamishri flew from Delhi to Bhavnagar in one of his planes. On the way Manavsingh asked Swamishri, “As a householder I do my duty of taking care of my family, but what is the true goal of life?” Swamishri replied, “God has endowed one with a human body, so one has to maintain one’s relationship with others in accordance with one’s karma. Our shastras prescribe that one should have the goal of attaining God while fulfilling one’s worldly duties. The final goal is to become atmarup and offer bhakti to Paramatma. If we so wish and desire for it then God will help us. One becomes blessed with the association of a Satpurush, and through satsang with him one attains mukti . So, to unshackle one’s soul from the bondage of maya and engage it in the service of God is the true goal of life.” Manavsingh: “To merely liberate one’s own soul, does it not amount to being selfish?” Swamishri: “No. The more we purify our inner self and realize the knowledge of atma, the more service we are able to offer selflessly and with perfection. One who is not selfish can help another better. So, by attaining knowledge of self ( atma-jnan) one can serve others properly.”
Remember god and make efforts

4 March 2009, Bhavnagar A student came to seek Swamishri’s blessings. Because of his academic burdens and pressures he had become depressed. As a result he slept all day. Whenever he sat down to read he felt sleepy and because of his depression his thoughts revolved around committing suicide. Swamishri reassured him, “There is no need to worry too much. Remember God and make efforts. If you fail you can study and re-take the exams. Don’t think of committing suicide!”
Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the assembly of the Pushpadolotsav (festival of colours). At the end of the assembly, pouring out the colour of his blessings, he said:

"There are two things: one is obeying commands, the other is upasana (correct understanding and worship of God). Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj have made our upasana very firm. But we will have to be very careful in obeying commands, because if a bird has two wings and one of them is weak, the bird drags itself along and cannot fly. Both wings must be equal; only then can it fly... Shriji Maharaj says, 'My words are my very form...' Since we have set out on this path, we must keep strength and courage. We must not get confused, we must not fall back... Just as Shriji Maharaj is in his abode, in the same way he has met us here too, in human form.

"Shriji Maharaj spoke countless talks for the liberation of souls. From these, Gunatitanand Swami drew out four: obeying commands, upasana, love for the God realised Sadhu, and friendliness towards devotees of God. And from these, Yogibapa pointed out just one thing, 'friendliness'. Everything is contained in it! Yogibapa used to say, 'In the future, friendliness will be dealt a blow.' Let us not let that happen... If we fall into negative feelings and seeing faults, it deals a big blow. Take special care in this matter. Otherwise one can come all the way down. Just as in snakes and ladders one can come down from 98 to 2."
Today in the assembly of the festival of colours, Swamishri scattered through his words the colours of loyalty to one's dharma, loyalty to the form of God, and loyalty to the fellowship.
